subject: Approximate mcmc samples using a smaller subset

messages.author: 77e72e34bf8c033f
messages.subject: Approximate mcmc samples using a smaller subset
parts:
Hi all

Is it possible to create a smaller set of mcmc samples, which approximately maintains the properties of the original joint posterior/mcmc samples? The most important properties to maintain are the MAP position and linear pairwise correlations between parameters.

I am interested in this as point estimates for my parameters (MAP, mean, median), do not reproduce the mean predictions of my models very well, and running the model on all the original mcmc samples is infeasible for my applications.

Thanks,
Per

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Approximate mcmc samples using a smaller subset
parts:
Not in general, see http://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01510.
Techniques like VP and EP can capture marginal expectations
like parameter means okay but they have trouble capturing
correlations — unfortunately if you want to model uncertainty
faithfully then you have to bite the bullet.

I won’t rant again here, but “MAP position” itself is ill-defined
and will make even less sense when you start messing about
with the size of the data set.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Approximate mcmc samples using a smaller subset
parts:
That is a slightly different but ultimately similar problem.

Formally MCMC generates samples to construct MCMC
estimators of expectations — the more samples the more
precise those estimators.  Given sufficient regularity
conditions the precision for an estimate is given by the
(Markov chain) Monte Carlo central limit theorem,

MCSE( E[f] ) = Var[f] / ESS

where Var[f] is the true variance of the function f and
ESS is the effective sample size which summarizes
the autocorrelations of your chain.  Var[f] is typically
estimated with MCMC itself (Stan does this
automatically), while ESS is estimated with using
an FFT-based autocorrelation estimator.

Anyways, the point is that you have to first define
what level of precision you need in your application
and then compute the variance of each estimator.
That defines the ESS you need.  If your posteriors
samples have a much larger ESS then you can thin
them (removing samples at equal intervals) until you
hit your ESS threshold, but that’s it.  If you need
serious precision then you’ll need all your samples.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Approximate mcmc samples using a smaller subset
parts:
You won't be able to recover the posterior mode (MAP
estimate) from a sample (set of draws from the posterior).
It's especially tricky in higher dimensions --- for a high
dimensional Gaussian, most of the posterior mass is not near
the posterior mode.

But if the joint posterior mode exists, you can run Stan's
optimizer to find it --- it's a much easier problem than
estimating the posterior mean computationally.

- Bob
